THE DEFECT. Decision P14 carried the trajectory as a block of exactly T epochs, each bundling its own joint state, action and reward. That carrier has NO coordinate for the state the last epoch transitions into. The core's kernel identity is a statement about \((Y_t,X_{t+1},H_{t+1})\) for every \(t=1,\ldots,T\), so at \(t=T\) the `histNextPair` projection had no \(S_{T+1}\) to project, and the only ways to type the compProd equation over that T-epoch block were (i) to drop the last epoch's kernel constraint, leaving the final transition unconstrained so that ass:pomdp-kernel no longer says what the core says, or (ii) to read the NEXT epoch's own state coordinate as the successor, which is a different and weaker statement at the last epoch and forces the state block to serve as both the current and the next state. Either way the two factorization predicates were not the core's, and the same conflation propagated into every projection built on them, into the tower/peeling steps of lem:radius-sensitive-phiw and into the witness laws. THE FIX: one carrier, one set of projections, and the entire S1/S2 closure re-derived from them. (1) THE CARRIER. `abbrev JointState (nX nH : Nat) := Fin nX x Fin nH`; `abbrev Step (nX nH : Nat) := R x JointState nX nH` -- the kernel target (reward VALUE and next joint state), i.e. the directive's `K : JointState -> Bool -> Measure (R x JointState)`, with rewards constrained to \([-1,1]\) by ass:bounded-reward; and `abbrev FullTrajectory (T nX nH : Nat) := (Fin (T + 1) -> JointState nX nH) x (Fin T -> Bool x R)`, whose first block is the state path \(S_1,\ldots,S_{T+1}\) and whose second block is the T epoch coordinates \((A_t,Y_t)\). `RawPomdpExperiment` carries `law : Measure (FullTrajectory T nX nH)` with `law_isProb`. Every earlier trajectory and epoch-block spelling is DELETED. (2) THE PROJECTIONS, against which every later equation is stated and only these: for `t : Fin T`, `curState t tau := tau.1 t.castSucc` is \(S_t\), `actionAt t tau := (tau.2 t).1` is \(A_t\), `rewardAt t tau := (tau.2 t).2` is \(Y_t\), and `nextState t tau := tau.1 t.succ` is \(S_{t+1}\) -- which now EXISTS for every t, at t = T-1 as `tau.1 (Fin.last T)`. Also `stateAt (i : Fin (T+1)) tau := tau.1 i`. Each is measurable by `measurable_pi_apply` composed with `Measurable.fst`/`Measurable.snd`, any tuple of them by `Measurable.prodMk` and any lambda into a pi type by `measurable_pi_lambda` (all four verified at round 10). (3) THE HISTORY VIEWS AND THE TWO FACTORIZATION PREDICATES, rebuilt against (2). `histStateView t tau := ((fun j : Fin t => tau.1 (j.castLE ..)), (fun j : Fin t => tau.2 (j.castLE ..)), tau.1 t.castSucc)` is the state-and-epoch history strictly before t together with the CURRENT joint state \(S_t\); `histActionPair t tau := (histStateView t tau, (tau.2 t).1)` adjoins \(A_t\); `histView t tau := histActionPair t tau` is the conditioning view of the kernel equation; and `histNextPair t tau := (histView t tau, ((tau.2 t).2, tau.1 t.succ))` adjoins the next BLOCK \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) in `Step nX nH`. Then `def PomdpKernelLaw (M) : Prop := (forall s a, IsProbabilityMeasure (M.K s a)) and forall t : Fin T, M.law.map (histNextPair t) = (M.law.map (histView t)).compProd (Kernel.comap (kernelOfK M) (currentStateAction t))`, where `currentStateAction t` reads \((S_t,A_t)\) off the history view; and `def SequentialIgnorability (M) : Prop := (M.b is a probability vector at each observed state) and forall t : Fin T, M.law.map (histActionPair t) = (M.law.map (histStateView t)).compProd (Kernel.comap (behaviourKernel M) (currentObsState t))`, where `currentObsState t` reads \(X_t\). BOTH quantify over EVERY `t : Fin T` with no exceptional last epoch -- that is the repair. `ass:stationary-start` compares the \(S_1\) marginal `M.law.map (stateAt 0)` with `M.init` cellwise on the finite joint state space and asks `M.init` to be invariant for `policyKernel M M.b`; the TERMINAL state carries no separate axiom, since its law is already determined by the kernel equation at t = T-1, which is exactly the core's content and is why no new model assumption appears. (4) THE OBSERVED SPACE. `abbrev ObsView (T nX : Nat) := Fin T -> (Fin nX x Bool x R)` is unchanged as a type and is now DEFINED by projecting the first T states and the T action/reward coordinates: `obsProj tau t := ((tau.1 t.castSucc).1, (tau.2 t).1, (tau.2 t).2)`. The TERMINAL state `tau.1 (Fin.last T)` is dropped, as is every latent coordinate; `obsLaw M := M.law.map obsProj` is a probability measure by `MeasureTheory.Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map_iff`. (5) THE ESTIMATOR CARRIER IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE ONLY ONE: `RawEstimator T := (nX : Nat) -> Policy nX -> Policy nX -> ObsView T nX -> R` and `ObservableEstimator T := { est : RawEstimator T // (forall nX b e w, est nX b e w in Set.Icc (-1 : R) 1) and (forall nX b e, Measurable (est nX b e)) }`, with `rawObservedRisk est M := Causalean.Stat.sqRisk (obsLaw M.raw) (est M.nX M.raw.b M.raw.e) (targetValue M.raw)` composing NO decoder. So `nR`, `rew`, the latent state, `M.K`, both stationary laws AND the terminal state are not estimator inputs -- by TYPING, not by a side condition. the round-8 reward decoder, the reward-coding field and the reward-value-invariance conjunct all stay DELETED from Basic.lean; the S2 reuse of `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` on the bounded carrier, its `hbdd` discharge, the constant-zero `Nonempty` witness and the whole P11 ledger (carrying P14 part (6)'s measurability and integrability premises on the raw side) are re-derived verbatim against this carrier. env.world: A single trajectory \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)_{t=1}^{T}\) from a time-homogeneous partially observed Markov decision process on a finite joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\) with binary action alphabet \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) and rewards bounded by one in absolute value. The primitives are a joint reward-transition kernel \(K(dy,dx',dh'\mid x,h,a)\), a known memoryless behavior policy \(b\) and a known memoryless target policy \(e\); derived from them are the policy-induced joint-state kernels \(P_p\), their stationary laws \(d_p\), the target-policy reward regression \(g_e\), the stationary target value \(\theta(K,e)\), and the observable one-step policy ratio \(\rho_t\). The regime parameters are the mixing scale \(t_0\), the log policy-overlap bound \(\zeta\) and the latent stationary-overlap radius \(C\), with derived constants \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\) and \(L=e^{\zeta}\). The latent coordinates \(H_t\), the joint states \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\) and both stationary laws are unobserved; only \(\mathsf O_T\) — the observed states \(X_t\), the actions \(A_t\) and the reward VALUES \(Y_t\in[-1,1]\) — together with \(b\), \(e\) and the observed alphabet is revealed. A trajectory of length \(T\) consists of the joint states \(S_1,\ldots,S_{T+1}\) together with the action-reward pairs \((A_t,Y_t)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\): at each epoch \(t\) the action is drawn from \(b(\cdot\mid X_t)\) and the kernel \(K\) generates the pair \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), so the terminal state \(S_{T+1}\) belongs to the trajectory while the observation records only the first \(T\) states, and of those only their observed coordinates. An estimator sees each epoch exactly through the triple \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)\): its argument is the sequence of those triples itself, and the reward enters only through its real value in \([-1,1]\). No restriction is placed on the reward law beyond that bound: the conditional law of \(Y_t\) under \(K\) may be any probability law on \([-1,1]\), discrete, continuous or mixed.
env.notes: Current P15 architecture. `JointState nX nH := Fin nX × Fin nH`. `Step nX nH := ℝ × JointState nX nH`. `FullTrajectory T nX nH := (Fin (T + 1) → JointState nX nH) × (Fin T → Bool × ℝ)`. `ObsView T nX := Fin T → (Fin nX × Bool × ℝ)` is the projection to `(X_t, A_t, Y_t)` from the first T states and the T action/reward coordinates; the terminal state is not observed. `K : JointState nX nH → Bool → Measure (ℝ × JointState nX nH)` has an arbitrary real reward law supported on `[-1,1]`. There is no class-level reward alphabet or coding map.

env.world: The observable-data decision problem attached to \(\mathrm S_1\). The cardinality-uniform experiment class \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) collects all such trajectory experiments, over unrestricted finite observed and latent alphabets, satisfying the seven class predicates. An estimator is any measurable function of \(\mathsf O_T\) — whose entries are the observed states, actions and reward values \(Y_t\in[-1,1]\) — together with \(b\), \(e\), \(t_0\), \(\zeta\), \(C\) and the observed alphabet, and the risk is squared error against \(\theta(K,e)\); \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the infimum over estimators of the supremum over the class, with comparison constants \(c_\star\le c^\star\) and threshold \(T_\star\). Because \(\theta(K,e)\in[-1,1]\), projecting an estimator onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase its squared error at any model, so every measurable estimator is dominated pointwise by a \([-1,1]\)-valued one; consequently the infimum over the \([-1,1]\)-valued estimators is at most the worst-case risk of any measurable estimator, and every lower bound proved against the restricted family holds pointwise against every measurable estimator. The competing family is taken to consist of the measurable \([-1,1]\)-valued functions of the trajectory of triples \(((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^{T}\) itself, together with \(b\), \(e\) and the regime parameters; this restricts the problem in no way that matters, because the candidate estimators below are of this form by construction, and each converse below is established pointwise against every measurable function of the trajectory whose mean squared error is finite at the two comparison models — an estimator with infinite mean squared error at one of them violates no risk lower bound. The candidate estimators are the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimators \(\widehat\theta_k\) built from the scores \(Z_t(k)=Y_t\prod_{j=t-k}^{t}\rho_j\), run at the balanced depth \(k_T\) or at the radius-adaptive depth \(\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)\). The rate parameters are the exponent \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), the normalized overlap radius \(q_C=(C-1)/C\), the shrinking overlap excess \(\delta_T\) defining the local radius \(C_T=1+\delta_T\), and the local-overlap derivation handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{loc}}\).
env.notes: Current P15 decision architecture plus P16 positive-horizon refinement. `ModelIndex T t0 zeta C` carries `horizon_pos : 1 ≤ T`, `nX`, `nH`, the raw experiment, and seven-predicate class membership. Horizon positivity is an environment constraint, not an eighth member of `LatentOverlapClass`. `RawEstimator T := (nX : Nat) → Policy nX → Policy nX → ObsView T nX → ℝ`. `ObservableEstimator T` is the subtype of such estimators that are measurable and `[-1,1]`-valued. Estimators receive only `nX`, revealed `b`, revealed `e`, and `ObsView`; they receive no reward-alphabet or coding data, latent-state data, kernel, stationary law, or terminal state. The regime parameters are closed over by `minimaxRisk`.

env.world: The signed-depth two-point sub-experiment inside \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) for \(C>1\). The observed state is constant, the hidden state is \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\) with depth \(J_t\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\) and sign \(U_t\in\{-1,+1\}\), the behavior policy plays action one with probability \(1/L\) and the target policy plays action one surely. A reset draws the sign with bias \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\); an advance retains the sign under action one and refreshes it under action zero; at terminal depth the reward is Rademacher with mean \(vc_0U_t\), where \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\) and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\) indexes the two alternatives. The depth marginal is stationary with masses \(w_j=(1-\alpha)\alpha^j/(1-\alpha^{Q+1})\), and the two induced observed-path laws are \(\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\). Attached to them is the observed filtration \(\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\sigma(A_1,Y_1,\ldots,A_{t-1},Y_{t-1})\), with observed prefix length \(\ell_t=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), predictive terminal posterior \(q_t^v=\Pr_v(J_t=Q\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\), rare-action-history factor \(a_t^{(Q)}\), and the two constants \(B_0\) (observed divergence) and \(K_0\) (uniform terminal posterior).

The diagnostic \(\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}\) is the difference between the stationary expectation of \(Y_te(A_t\mid X_t)/b(A_t\mid X_t)\) and \(\theta(K,e)\) in this model.

ass:pomdp-kernel.notes: Modeling assumption (causal-structural): a restriction on the data law. ROUND-10 SPELLING (decision P15 parts (1)-(3), which REPLACES the round-9 T-epoch trajectory spelling -- deleted, not amended -- and which itself replaced the round-1 positive-mass-prefix spelling, since conditioning on atoms is meaningless once the reward is real-valued): `def PomdpKernelLaw (M : RawPomdpExperiment T nX nH) : Prop` says (i) K is a Markov kernel, `forall s a, IsProbabilityMeasure (M.K s a)`, and (ii) for EVERY epoch `t : Fin T` the joint law of the history-and-next-block factorizes as a composition product, `M.law.map (histNextPair t) = (M.law.map (histView t)).compProd (Kernel.comap (kernelOfK M) (currentStateAction t))`, where the projections are taken off `FullTrajectory T nX nH := (Fin (T + 1) -> JointState nX nH) x (Fin T -> Bool x R)`: `histView t` is the state-and-epoch history strictly before t together with the current \(S_t = \)`tau.1 t.castSucc` and the current action \(A_t = (\)`tau.2 t`\().1\), and `histNextPair t` pairs that history with the next block \((Y_t, S_{t+1}) = ((\)`tau.2 t`\().2, \)`tau.1 t.succ`\()\) in `Step nX nH`. WHY THE ROUND-9 SPELLING WAS WRONG (the flagged defect): the round-9 T-epoch block had no coordinate for \(S_{T+1}\), so at the last epoch the equation could only be dropped (a strictly weaker predicate than the core's) or re-read against the next epoch's own state (a different statement). With the T+1-state block `nextState t` exists for every t, so this predicate is EXACTLY the core's conditional-law identity for \(t = 1,\ldots,T\), stated as an equality of measures instead of a statement about atoms, and it is the form the reused KL chain rule and the reused tower lemma `MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_compProd` consume directly. No new model assumption is added -- the terminal state gets no axiom of its own; its law is determined by this equation at t = T-1. Time homogeneity is still automatic because K carries no time index. The projections are measurable by `measurable_pi_apply`, `Measurable.fst`/`Measurable.snd` and `Measurable.prodMk` (re-verified at round 10). Threaded, never discharged: the note declares it an atomic assumption. def:phiw-estimator.notes: `def ratio (b e : Fin nX -> Bool -> R) (x : Fin nX) (a : Bool) : R := if b x a = 0 then 0 else e x a / b x a` realizes rho_t with the zero-cell convention; `def phiwScore (k : Nat) (b e : Policy nX) (w : ObsView T nX) (t : Fin T) : R` realizes Z_t(k) = Y_t * prod over j in [t-k, t] of rho_j, with Y_t := (w t).2.2 -- the DECODED reward value carried by the observation itself, which is the round-8 spelling of decision P13 -- and rho_j := ratio b e (w j).1 (w j).2.1; `def phiwEstimator (k : Nat) (b e : Policy nX) : ObsView T nX -> R := clipUnit ((T-k)^{-1} * sum over t > k of phiwScore ...)`. Two derived forms are used: the UNCLIPPED average (called `phiwRaw`, on which bias and variance are computed) and the clipped estimator, linked by the one-line lemma 'projection onto [-1,1] cannot increase squared distance to a target in [-1,1]'. REVISED at F2.5: because the estimator carrier of decision P3 PASSES b and e, `phiwEstimator k` can be coerced into the estimator carrier at all -- under the previous policy-blind carrier that was impossible without fixing one policy pair for the whole class, since rho_t is a function of (b, e). S1 world carriers: JointState := Fin nX x Fin nH, Step := R x JointState nX nH, FullTrajectory := (Fin (T + 1) -> JointState nX nH) x (Fin T -> Bool x R), ObsView := Fin T -> (Fin nX x Bool x R); the epoch projections stateAt / curState (tau.1 t.castSucc) / nextState (tau.1 t.succ) / actionAt / rewardAt and their measurability lemmas; obsProj tau t := ((tau.1 t.castSucc).1, (tau.2 t).1, (tau.2 t).2) (first T states, observed coordinate only, plus the T action/reward coordinates, dropping the terminal state and every latent coordinate); RawPomdpExperiment with K : JointState -> Bool -> Measure (Step ..), b, e, init, law : Measure (FullTrajectory ..) and law_isProb; obsLaw := law.map obsProj; kernelOfK; the history/next-block views histStateView / histActionPair / histView / histNextPair and the readers currentObsState / currentStateAction used by the factorization predicates; behaviourKernel, policyKernel (marginalizing the reward via {q : Step | q.2 = s'}), tvNorm, stationaryLaw, rewardRegression as an integral, ratio; the seven assumption Prop defs in their round-10 spelling (compProd factorization for PomdpKernelLaw and SequentialIgnorability, quantified over EVERY t : Fin T against the projections above; the S_1 marginal via stateAt 0 for StationaryStart; the K-level real bound for BoundedReward; the other three unchanged); LatentOverlapClass; targetValue; overlapRadius; clipUnit; phiwScore/phiwRaw/phiwEstimator/phiwObservable (all on the observed path ObsView, taking no reward coding map); historyDepth; radiusAdaptiveDepth; Policy; RawEstimator ((nX : Nat) -> Policy nX -> Policy nX -> ObsView T nX -> R); ObservableEstimator (the subtype carrier with the [-1,1] bound of decision P7 (ii) and the measurability conjunct of decision P13; round-7's reward-value-invariance predicate stays DELETED and F2 must not emit it); clipEst (total on measurable raw estimators, taking `hmeas : forall nX b e, Measurable (est nX b e)`); ModelIndex (nX nH only, no nR); rawObservedRisk (no decoder composed in); observedRisk; minimaxRisk; and the round-6 fidelity ledger (decision P11) that REPLACES the withdrawn equality minimaxRisk_eq_rawMinimaxRisk -- which F2 must NOT emit, since Causalean.Stat.worstCaseRisk returns the junk value 0 for a raw estimator with unbounded risk (MinimaxValue.lean:49-50) and so a raw minimaxValue is not def:minimax-risk's inf-sup: namely minimaxRisk_le_rawWorstCaseRisk (for every MEASURABLE raw est whose risk range is BddAbove over the class, minimaxRisk <= Causalean.Stat.worstCaseRisk (rawObservedRisk ..) est, via minimaxValue_le_worstCaseRisk_of_nonneg at clipEst est hmeas then worstCaseRisk_le composed with le_worstCaseRisk), resting on the Helpers/Kernels.lean pointwise domination clipEst_observedRisk_le. The measurability premise on that ledger lemma is the round-8 correction (decision P13) and REPLACES round-7's reward-value-invariance premise: it is literally the note's own admissibility clause, so the ledger dominates exactly def:minimax-risk's estimator family. ROUND-9 (decision P14 part (6)): that ledger lemma additionally carries per-model integrability of the raw squared loss, since Causalean.Stat.sqRisk is a bare Bochner integral and returns the junk value 0 for a non-integrable loss on the now-infinite observed space; both premises are automatic on the carrier and are the honest exclusion of Lean's integration convention, exactly parallel to P11's BddAbove premise. ROUND-10 (decision P15): the only additions to this file are the epoch projections and their measurability lemmas (measurable_pi_apply / Measurable.fst / Measurable.snd / Measurable.prodMk / measurable_pi_lambda); the round-9 trajectory types and every earlier carrier spelling are DELETED, and line count is raised slightly for the projection layer.

ROUND-9 ADDITION (decision P14 part (5)), RESPELLED AT ROUND 10 (decision P15 part (6)): the witness-construction device that keeps every finite computation in this plan intact while the CLASS stays the core's full real-reward class, now on the same two-block trajectory shape as the class. `FiniteTrajectory T nX nH nR` is the Fintype pairing a `Fin (T + 1)`-indexed joint-state block with the T (action, reward-symbol) epoch coordinates; `FiniteObsView T nX nR` is the matching T-epoch observed-symbol view; `structure FiniteRewardModel (T nX nH nR : Nat)` carries a PMF-valued kernel into pairs of a reward symbol and the next joint state, a value map carrying each reward symbol to its real value in [-1,1], init, b, e and law : PMF (FiniteTrajectory T nX nH nR) built by the epoch fold (PMF.bind over Fin.induction, snocing each drawn next state onto the state block -- Fin.snoc / Fin.snoc_castSucc / Fin.snoc_last / Fin.init_snoc); together with its finite derived objects (finObsProj, obsPMF := law.map finObsProj, the finite policyKernel, the finite target value) and the decoder decodeTraj (identity on the state block, recoding only the reward symbol; measurable for free from discreteness). `noncomputable def embed (F : FiniteRewardModel T nX nH nR) : RawPomdpExperiment T nX nH` pushes K forward under (fun p => (F.rew p.1, p.2)) and law forward under decodeTraj F.rew. Then the bridge lemmas, each proved ONCE and consumed by all three witness families: embed_pomdpKernelLaw, embed_sequentialIgnorability, embed_stationaryStart, embed_boundedReward (from a pointwise bound on F.rew), embed_policyKernel_eq and embed_stationaryLaw_eq (the finite kernel and both stationary laws are unchanged by the embedding -- this is why every membership, contraction and overlap verification stays the finite computation it was), embed_targetValue_eq (the pushed-forward reward kernel's mean integral collapses to the finite sum), embed_obsLaw_eq, embed_absolutelyContinuous (over Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.map, transporting each hard pair's finite full-support discharge of hac) and embed_klDiv_le (over Mathlib InformationTheory.klDiv_map_le, the data-processing inequality, transporting each finite KL budget to the real-reward observed law in the <= direction the converses need, which also yields hfin). SEARCH TRACE for the two transport lemmas is in the S1 and lem:observed-path-kl round-9 traces; no Causalean or Mathlib decl packages a finite-to-general reward-encoding bridge for trajectory experiments, so this file is paper-local build-inline and small. ROUND-10 (decision P15 part (6)): because decodeTraj is the IDENTITY on the state block, every bridge lemma is re-proved against the round-10 projections with no change in content; the epoch fold is what makes the witness laws satisfy the kernel predicate at EVERY epoch, including the last, and the line count is raised for the fold's Fin.snoc bookkeeping.
